column8: Sun 22 Nov: store, input to row 29: Yang lost money on comics for about ten years before 2006; one creator's own account, never about Laura.
Sun 22 Nov: store, input to row 29: a teacher's wage carried Yang's book income through 2001 and 2008-09; never imply Laura has a day job (the case says nothing of one).
Sun 22 Nov: store: near the top of the field book income still did not replace a day job (Yang, 2014); an opinion in a magazine piece, colour only.
Sun 22 Nov: store, input to row 30: a licence 17 years after the book, cancelled in a share boom; Variety's reason rests on an unnamed source.
Sun 22 Nov: store: a named 2020 case beside Q12-035 and Q1-033 (events stop first and completely); the survey rows carry the point, this one only names it.
Sun 22 Nov: store: a creator's income slid for a decade with no share fall (her outlets closed), so lumpy and its own weather; refines IPS l.9, never as if l.9 were wrong.

Sun 22 Nov: 2.3 reservoir for 'lumpy' (row 35's added leg): one book contract worth about a decade of steady strip income, in the creator's own words; her estimate, no dollar figure, never about Laura.
Sun 22 Nov: store, input to row 30: a stage licence lifted a nine-year-old book in a year set by a theatre award, not the economy.
Sun 22 Nov: store: a celebrated career's biggest prize arrived as five years of fixed quarterly sums and went to debt and retirement; a prize is no plannable income.

Sun 22 Nov: 3a reserve only: an artists' funder chose fixed sums on known dates over years; 3a's one outside parallel is the lottery rule (ARGUMENT_TREE Branch 2), and the MacArthur pays from its own endowment, so never 'endowment' for her reserve.

Sun 22 Nov: store, input to row 30: Persepolis took off in the 2001-02 slump because the news made Iran a subject; a big piece on its own clock, never evidence that her income rises when shares fall (row 32).
Sun 22 Nov: store: adaptation money is committed years ahead by pre-sales; gross is not her income and her share is not public.
Sun 22 Nov: store, input to row 29: Maus was paid for by a day job at Topps one day a week.
Sun 22 Nov: store: the Pulitzer book's advance was small; NPR transcript extract, no amount.
Sun 22 Nov: store: one classic's backlist pays like an annuity; one book in a generation, so never 'her income is bond-like' (ARGUMENT_TREE Branch 1: no beta, no steady link).

Sun 22 Nov: 2.3 reservoir for the own-clock leg: Maus print sales rose 8.5 times in a week after a school board's ban in a year the S&P fell 18.04%; use +753% or 8.5 times, never Forbes's +46% for week 2 (44%, Keel arithmetic); a ban usually cuts school buying (row 28).
Sun 22 Nov: store, input to row 29: work on another author's series carried Telgemeier through 2006-09.
Sun 22 Nov: store: the large income came in the 2010s boom from a book signed in the slump; a first printing is a bet, not sales; extracts.
Sun 22 Nov: twin of Q56-016 (a book's money is front-loaded, 96% of a bestseller's sales in year one); adds one children's title's -33% and -37% in years two and three (Keel arithmetic).

Sun 22 Nov: 2.3 and store, the guard behind the Q215 overrides: one creator's backlist fell 5.3% and 7.4% while her category grew 15% in 2020, so a category is not a creator; never use shelf growth as her income (sums Keel arithmetic).

Sun 22 Nov: 3e area 2 and 2.3: for classroom authors (case p.1) the money schools pay fell 57% in the shock year (Scholastic's US fairs, FY2021); publisher revenue, not royalties, and a fall while shares rose, so 'later and smaller' for school money, never a share link.

Sun 22 Nov: 2.3 reservoir: in one creator's 2020 book money more than doubled while every trip went, which pins 'later and smaller' to the event stream; 'at least 2.2 times' is Keel inference from the lists' 100,000 cut-off; prize and lockdown reading mixed.
Sun 22 Nov: store, input to row 29: twenty years of a one-person press before the prize, and a film option only after it.

Sun 22 Nov: store: kids' graphic novels grew 13% across channels in 2020 (15% in the book channel); a category, not a creator (row 20), and never evidence that her income rose when shares fell (row 32).
Sun 22 Nov: store: children's digital library loans rose 79% in 2020 through per-loan licences; loans are not author income and the 400-500% is one librarian's.
Sun 22 Nov: store: San Diego Comic-Con cancelled for the first time in 50 years (2020); the organiser's income, beside rows 5 and 22 for events at zero.
Sun 22 Nov: store, extends Q1-034 and Q12-021: in January 2009, 54% of school librarians expected 2009-10 cuts; expectations from self-selected respondents, not outcomes.

Sun 22 Nov: 3e area 2 reservoir: in October 2026 an agency for 80+ children's authors reported far fewer 2026-27 school visits (enrolment, insurance, bans), so the speaking stream behind the 2028 deposit can shrink without a recession; one agency, never Laura's own bookings.

Sun 22 Nov: 2.3 reservoir (card's best two): all six paid for the breakthrough with other work, so creators spread their careers before their portfolios; a survivor sample, and the case names Laura's streams but no day job, so never say she has one.
Sun 22 Nov: 2.3: the big pieces came in slumps and booms alike, so they neither cushion nor double her share risk; event dates, not payment dates, a small sample.

Sun 22 Nov: 2.3, the evidence for 'lumpy': one contract, one week, one first decade; swings in sales are not swings in income, so never set a week's multiple beside the S&P's worst year as like for like, and never a beta (Q1-049's note).

Sun 22 Nov: 2.3, backs ARGUMENT_TREE Branch 1's 'not bond-like either': tested across shelf, school, library and events, no stream rose because shares fell; kills 'countercyclical' (overrides on Q1-032, Q1-046, Q1b-022, Q12b-001, Q56-020, Q148-014).

Sun 22 Nov: 2.3 and 3e area 2: the case's sources for the 2028 deposit (advances, speaking, licensing, other ventures, p.2) are exactly IPS l.9's three, the streams the class shows coming later and smaller, so 2.3 can say why l.9 names them; steadier backlist royalties are not named.

Sun 22 Nov: 2.3 (D4): most of a graphic memoirist's risk is her own, and background risk (Q206 rows 1-2) says even an independent risk argues for caution, so the case for Treasuries needs only 'can come later and smaller'; Treasuries stop the payments depending on the career, never hedge it (Q206-028).

Sun 22 Nov: 2.3 wording note: keeps l.9's three streams, adds lumpiness and the Census -7.8% (never -11.6%); fix 'comes later and smaller in the same slumps' to 'can come later and smaller in the same slumps' (D4: 'can', never a measured link), and cite the unsellable-holding clause as the IPS's own, not new.

Sun 22 Nov: 3d's must-never list and 3e's one limit: the US residencies' own alliance says a residency's success is not easily measured, so the report promises co-sponsors no measured effect on residents, only the money; 2010, before the first lottery study.
Sun 22 Nov: store, second voice behind row 1: 89% of 18 arts councils fund residencies, 38% evaluated, none could share a report; 2013 self-selected survey.
Sun 22 Nov: store: the 84% are artists' own reports with no comparison group; never as an effect.
Sun 22 Nov: store: about eight applications per North American place (2012), so selection is the first suspect behind any alumni record (row 21).
Sun 22 Nov: store, input to row 34: a small residency's best practice is a follow-up survey over three years; excerpts of the PDFs only.
Sun 22 Nov: store: two reviews find the effect of artist support unmeasured; WolfBrown read at source, Lehman's words secondhand (abstract only), so never quote Lehman.

Sun 22 Nov: store: residencies are 'necessary and insufficient' and the literature grades its own homework; interpretive sociology; book title and initials unconfirmed, so complete the citation before any use.
Sun 22 Nov: store: France's national survey calls residencies' effect on careers 'equivocal'; an open questionnaire.
Sun 22 Nov: store: hosts select on notoriety (a Matthew effect), which is why alumni lists flatter residencies; French visual artists only.

Sun 22 Nov: store: artists judge a residency first by its money (77%); the ten pay operating expenses (case p.3), not necessarily artists' grants, and say 'held for her in Treasuries', never 'owned' as the gloss.

Sun 22 Nov: store, behind the must-never list: the only near-miss test of a famous residency finds the chosen modestly ahead of the nearly chosen, mixing the jury's eye with the stay; never in the report as an effect.

Sun 22 Nov: store pedigree for VT's reason (Trading Note 3, the vain illusion that we can pick winners): the jury beat a lottery by gains the authors call small; 3f takes no outside parallel (D16) and the report never repeats the Trading Notes, so never in prose or Laura's words.
Sun 22 Nov: store: no general Venice effect on careers (98 artists, before and after, no control); a showcase, not a residency.

Sun 22 Nov: store; the cleanest randomised evidence on what reliable money gives artists (about four more hours a week of art, New York, 18 months); cash, not a residency, and no slot (3d's parallel is Spelman and Lehman; D11 puts funders' words before the lab).
Sun 22 Nov: store, behind row 14: the money bought time, not income (outside earnings fell about as much as was paid).
Sun 22 Nov: store: the same lottery raised self-reported experimentation and skill; abstract and excerpts.

Sun 22 Nov: store: connected peers nearby go with about 15% more lasting works (fixed-effects panel, historical writers); fits the case's 'collaborative' only as background, never as an outcome for her residents.
Sun 22 Nov: store: higher arts pay can mean fewer arts hours (Australian data), so a residency's effect depends on who comes.
Sun 22 Nov: store: a grant's value is partly the signal of being chosen, which a residency opening in 2033 does not yet have.
Sun 22 Nov: store: support follows reputation in Flemish grants; abstract and highlights.
Sun 22 Nov: 3d must-never list: alumni prize tallies count whom a residency chose and grow with time, never what it did; Slate's counts unverified.
Sun 22 Nov: store only: IWP's Taiwan founding thread is context, never a reason for Laura or 'why Taiwan' (the case gives none).

Sun 22 Nov: 3a reserve behind the lottery rule and Oman (GIA 2018): a 58-year residency lost about half its operating budget when one outside funder's grants ended in 2025, which is why IPS l.11 rests the ten on no one else's money; one clause at most, never a second parallel.

Sun 22 Nov: 3d reserve behind Spelman and Lehman (aha 8, card Q200): in 2025 awarded grants were withdrawn mid-grant with the money spent, so a grant awarded is a promise to pay and Treasuries held for her are money; never in Laura's words.
Sun 22 Nov: twin of Q11d-003 (public arts money pays after the work, while Laura's cash arrives first); adds US federal reimbursement from one newspaper report.
Sun 22 Nov: store, beside Q9b-017 and GOLDMINE 15: a 13-year residency suspended for lost funding while a tenant on others' land; the case's two asks, early running money and a building.
Sun 22 Nov: store: a flood hit a residency's building (2023); insurance and repairs not costed, so not an overrun figure.
Sun 22 Nov: store: AIR Taipei's own reports give about 600 and more than 500 artists hosted, so the report states no count of Taiwan's residents.

Sun 22 Nov: 3d background, store: Taiwan's Ministry scores funded villages on operations, space use and budget execution, never residents' careers, so co-sponsors judge how a residency is run and paid for.
Sun 22 Nov: store: about one Taiwanese overseas-residency applicant in five went in 2017; one year, outbound.
Sun 22 Nov: store: Taiwan's studies of residents are qualitative or self-reported; side jobs crowd out residency time.
Sun 22 Nov: store: public money dominates Taiwan's residencies, so one whose running money is its founder's is the less common kind; a 2008 view, and her co-sponsors may still bring public money.
Sun 22 Nov: store: Western residency evidence comes from old, selective programmes with prestige to lend, so the report borrows no other residency's results.
Sun 22 Nov: 3d's order: the residency opens in 2033 and career effects take 3 to 10 years to measure, so in 2031 Laura can show co-sponsors her money, not results.
Sun 22 Nov: store: the exact sentence for row 14 if the team ever wants one; no slot in Section 3 (3d's one parallel is Spelman and Lehman, D6), never in Laura's words, never with a career claim.
Sun 22 Nov: process: the register's FRED mirror holds 1983-93 complete (8l already verified all 516 months), so the 1985-92 rise was in the data and the windows left it out.
Sun 22 Nov: 3e background, store: the dated path of the 1985-92 rise; 63.5% peak to low is Keel arithmetic not in NUMBERS (CBC 63.3%, Q10b daily 65.7%), so register it before use.

Sun 22 Nov: 3e's hard case (ARGUMENT_TREE Branch 6, waiting): +38.3% from the currency alone, Jan 1986 to Jan 1988, 2.3 times the largest currency move since 1991; not in NUMBERS until the numbers owner registers it (section 9, Sun 22 Nov evening); fix the row's '29.0% highest joint rise since 1991': 29.0% is the top of the 30 strong-NT$ windows, and the highest joint since 1991 is 38.9% (8q).

Sun 22 Nov: Table 3 row 7's note and NUMBERS wording (section 9 items 1 and 3): 8j's moves start in October 1986 and 8q's windows in 1991 because the national building-cost index starts then; say 'since 1991' with that reason every time, so the start reads as the data's, not chosen.
Sun 22 Nov: store: 37 of 87 windows from 1983-90 starts were 10%+ stronger; overlapping windows of one episode, never odds (Q210), and Keel arithmetic not in NUMBERS.
Sun 22 Nov: store: the joint rise on Taipei City's index (+48.1%, highest +50.4%) is a city series, never set beside 8q's national figures as like for like; Keel arithmetic, unregistered.

Sun 22 Nov: 3e's limit, waiting for NUMBERS (section 9 item 2): +38.3% on $115,000 needs about $44,045, $15,363 beyond $28,682 (8q), falling on the building's NT$ budget, never the ten or the range; about the size of 8q's registered worst (+38.9%, $44,756), so say a second episode beyond her flexibility, never 'far larger'.

Sun 22 Nov: Table 3 row 7's note: from the August 1985 level a 10% watch fires in October 1986 with most of the move still to come, so a trigger, never a size; 10.5%, 33.7% and 41.2% are Keel arithmetic, unregistered.
Sun 22 Nov: store: the rise began from a rate held at 36-40 for years and near its weakest in decades in 1985.
Sun 22 Nov: store: the first condition, a current-account surplus near 14% of GNP over 1983-88, over 20% in 1986.
Sun 22 Nov: store: under capital controls the surplus piled up as central-bank reserves.
Sun 22 Nov: store: the CBC chose a slow, announced rise, which drew hot money; Taiwan's own account, extract.
Sun 22 Nov: store, behind row 8: a slow rise invited a one-way bet, why a 10% move can keep going; Xu read in abstract only.
Sun 22 Nov: store, for any cause clause: 'after the Plaza Accord, under pressure from the US Treasury', sharpening from August 1986.
Sun 22 Nov: store: the 1986 Section 301 cases were market access, so never 'Section 301 forced the rise'; Business Today's 1989 claim conflicts with the Treasury record.
Sun 22 Nov: store: the currency lever was the Treasury under Section 3004 of the 1988 Act (Taiwan named Oct 1988, Apr 1989, May and Dec 1992); extract.
Sun 22 Nov: store: Treasury's own count, the NT$ 49% stronger since Plaza by April 1989; a source's figure, never a register one.
Sun 22 Nov: store: Treasury found manipulation again in 1992, the 1991-92 leg.
Sun 22 Nov: store: GAO's 29 percent (1985-88) is the stricter convention, never beside 8j's 29.4% or the 29.0% of the strong windows; 'about 39%' in 8j's convention is Keel arithmetic, unregistered.

Sun 22 Nov: store: AIT's flat US-dollar budget met a 14% fall against the NT$ in FY1988 and its exchange programme shrank about 20%, the case in miniature; 3e's one parallel is the gilt crisis (D6), so never a second; one think-tank source.
Sun 22 Nov: store: Japan's host government took on part of US forces' yen costs in 1987; a local-currency partner does not lose from a stronger currency; yen, a government.
Sun 22 Nov: store: the rise reshaped Taiwan's exports and jobs; background.
Sun 22 Nov: store: Taiwan's share index rose about ninefold 1986-89 and fell up to 80% in 1990 (index base not stated, so never quote the levels).
Sun 22 Nov: store: the CBC's record NT$240bn exchange loss (year to June 1987) is secondary and UNVERIFIED; never in the report.

Sun 22 Nov: 3e could-it-recur clause, store: the surplus is about a fifth of output again but now leaves through private investors; 'about two-thirds above 2025' is Keel arithmetic on first releases since revised, unregistered; no forecast.
Sun 22 Nov: store: Taiwan on Treasury's monitoring list (Jun 2025, Jan and Jul 2026), meeting two criteria; a list, not a manipulation finding.
Sun 22 Nov: store: the NT$ weakened in November 2026 (32.947 on 18 Nov); the register's 32.768 on 6 Nov stays 8d's base, and a month says nothing about 2031.
Sun 22 Nov: 3e, one clause at most: a large surplus and US scrutiny are back, the daily limit, capital controls and reserve-piling are gone; could recur, no forecast; never VT as a hedge.

Sun 22 Nov: store: on Taipei City's index costs rose about 7% while the currency rose 38% in 1986-88, and about 20% a year later, so a currency watch can fire before costs show; city index, Keel arithmetic, unregistered.
Sun 22 Nov: store: cheaper imports softened exporters' loss 1985-89; not measured for building (row 29).

Sun 22 Nov: 3e's hard case form, waiting for NUMBERS: Q210's four dated episodes since 1991 'and, before them, 1986-88'; say the largest currency move on record (38.3%), since on the joint measure 1986-88 is larger than 2006-08's 38.9% only on Taipei City's index; never '1 in 20', never the 1980s windows as odds.
Sun 22 Nov: twin of Q10e-025 (the currency's link with US shares, -0.39 to 2000 and +0.32 since, averaging about +0.09); VT is never a Taiwan-dollar hedge.

Sun 22 Nov: store: the 2020 category figures check, but drop the use line 'Laura's own genre boomed in the crash year': shares rose 18% in 2020, a category is not a creator and no stream rose because shares fell (card Q215 rows 20, 24, 32); keep PreK-12 -19.6% as the school leg.

Sun 22 Nov: 2.3, case fact only: Laura published The Wuhan I Know in 2020 (case p.1); drop 'its best year so far came when markets crashed' (the case gives no income by year) and read it with card Q215 row 30: a career's big pieces keep their own clock, neither cushion nor double share risk; 'later and smaller' for new money (D4).

Sun 22 Nov: store: drop 'can move against shares' and 'grew strongly in a year shares fell': card Q215 row 32 finds no stream that rose because shares fell (its own weather), and the series is mostly performers, 2020 a lockdown; never evidence of writers' income rising when shares fall.

Sun 22 Nov: 3e store: the non-manga shelf grew in 2008-09 (checks), but a shelf is not a creator's income (card Q215 row 20) and school-paid money fell after both shocks (rows 21, 27, 32); say its own weather, never that her part of the market grew through the recession as if it rose when shares fell.

Sun 22 Nov: store only: deal counts (blog copy, unverified) are not income, advances are paid in pieces and were stretched in 2020 (Q206), and card Q215 rows 22 and 32 show event money gone and no stream rising because shares fell; never 'her corner of the market grew fastest in the shock year'.

Sun 22 Nov: 3e store: the employer wage bill rose in 2008, 2018 and 2022 while shares fell, but it is companies with staff, not a writer, and card Q215 row 32 kills any countercyclical reading (no stream rose because shares fell); say its own timing; the career figure stays the Census -7.8% for one-person artists' and writers' 2009 receipts, never -11.6%.

Sun 22 Nov: 2.3 reservoir: keep the participation finding as quoted, but never 'an uncorrelated income argues for more shares': card Q215 row 34 with Q206 rows 1-2 (background risk, Kimball) says an independent risk still leaves a cautious investor wanting fewer; the certainty requirement carries the ladder either way.

Sun 22 Nov: Table 3 row 7's note or 3e: 8j's largest +29.4% holds only on 8j's own windows, whose moves start in October 1986 (card Q217 rows 3-4), so say so and never 'the largest two-year move (+29.4%, 1986-88)' or 'since 1983' for the moves; the series' largest is +38.3%, Jan 1986 to Jan 1988 (Keel arithmetic, not yet in NUMBERS); drop '1-in-20 +13.7%' (D7); 98.3% as a share of windows, never odds.

Sun 22 Nov: 3b, 3e and Table 3 row 7: add 'since 1991' with its reason (Taiwan's national building-cost index starts then): the 30 windows, median 22.3% and range 9.3% to 29.0% are since 1991, and the 1986-88 rise, 38.3% from the currency alone, came before them and was larger (card Q217 rows 3-4, unregistered); figures match 8q's Q131 block.

Sun 22 Nov: 3e store: 'the strongest case of both risks at once' only among the strong-NT$ windows since 1991 (card Q217 rows 3-4: the 1986-88 currency alone rose 38.3%, before the national index); figures reproduce.
Sun 22 Nov: store: 'the joint worst of the strong-NT$ windows' since 1991 only, the national index's start (card Q217 rows 3-4); the 1986-88 currency alone rose 38.3%; figures reproduce.

Sun 22 Nov: 3b: the worst strong-NT$ window (+29.0%, about $33,400) is the worst since 1991 only (card Q217 rows 3-4; 1986-88's currency alone needs about $44,045, Q217 row 7, unregistered); the $25,600 and $33,400 needs are now reproduced in 8q's Q131 block; $28,682 and 24.9% check.

Sun 22 Nov: store: 16.9% (Feb 2009 to Feb 2011) is the NT$'s largest two-year rise since 1991 only; the series' largest is +38.3%, Jan 1986 to Jan 1988 (card Q217 row 3, Keel arithmetic, unregistered), not 8j's +29.4%, which starts in November 1986 because 8j's windows start in October 1986.

Sun 22 Nov: FACTS_PLAIN l.100 and 3e: keep the episode form, but 8j's real-currency moves start in October 1986, not 1983 (card Q217 row 4), so say 'since late 1986', and never 'never short once anything above the top is counted' without that date: the Jan 1986 to Jan 1988 rise would leave about $15,400 short (Q217 row 7, Keel arithmetic, waiting for NUMBERS); 'VT bought' never before 2008.
